Subject: Follow-up & next steps — deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Alicia / Carlos —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Nova Health's roadmap and the ML infra constraints you're working with. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:  

Recap (what I heard)
- You're migrating away from a mix of a legacy GPU cluster + some self-hosted LLM endpoints (fine-tuned models) and evaluating options to standardize inference.
- Key constraints: PHI handling, SOC 2 compliance, data residency (US), predictable latency for clinical workflows (~100–200ms p50), and predictable unit economics for payor integrations.
- Pilot timeline: target 3-month pilot starting Q3; procurement requires a ballpark cost and proposed deployment model for approval.

Options to evaluate (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest to launch, Redwood-managed, quickest integration — data-in-transit controls and options for in-region hosting, but not ideal for PHI without dedicated isolation.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools, per-customer isolation and SLA-backed throughput/latency — good middle ground for predictable cost and faster onboarding than private.
- Private VPC / On‑prem: full network isolation, customer-managed networking & KMS — best match for regulated PHI use cases but longer procurement and ops timeline.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short deployment comparison doc and the questionnaire you requested (we captured a few technical items to speed the architecture review).

Next steps
1) Attached: redwood-deployment-comparison.pdf and nova-msp-questions.xlsx (please fill or confirm answers where possible).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our solutions engineer (Marcus) and security lead (David) — proposed slots: Wed 16 Jun 11:00 PT or Thu 17 Jun 09:00 PT.
3) If you can share expected QPS / concurrency and an example throughput window (e.g., 200 reqs/min peak, avg 5k req/day), we can put together a pilot cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private.

If that all looks good I’ll lock the deep-dive and kick off a short internal pricing exercise.

Best,

Hi Alicia —

Great context — appreciate the clear constraints. I attached the deployment-comparison PDF above; here’s a concise comparison focused on your requirements and the pilot sizing you shared: 

- Hosted API (Redwood-managed): Pros — fastest to market, low integration lift, predictable request-based billing. Cons — not ideal for PHI unless paired with Dedicated isolation or VPC networking add-ons.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): Pros — per-customer isolation, in-region hosting, SLA-backed throughput and latency, supports KMS integration. Good trade-off if you want isolation without full on‑prem procurement. Cons — monthly commit required; lead time for capacity scheduling (typically 2–4 weeks).
- Private VPC / On‑prem: Pros — full control of network and data, customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), best for PHI workflows. Cons — longer procurement/onboarding (4–10 weeks), enterprise license and support fees, ops responsibilities on your side.

For the pilot assumptions you listed (5 concurrent users, 3k–7k req/day, avg 200 tokens per request), I’ll ask Marcus to produce a pair of estimates: a) Dedicated (monthly reserved cap) and b) Private (one-time onboarding + monthly platform fee).

Proposed next step: Technical deep-dive with Marcus + David — can you confirm Wed 16 Jun 11:00 PT? I’ll send a calendar invite and include a brief agenda: 1) architecture options & network diagram, 2) KMS & SOC2 controls, 3) pilot measurement & SLOs, 4) procurement timeline.

Also: could you attach a short list of allowed IP ranges / firewall constraints for the pilot so Marcus can prepare the network diagram?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa
